claude.name: Claude
claude.description: Anthropic Claude models via Claude CLI - specialized expert subagents

codex.name: Codex (GPT)
codex.description: OpenAI GPT models via Codex CLI - specialized expert subagents

agy.name: Agy
agy.description: Google Antigravity CLI - Gemini, Claude and GPT-OSS models as specialized expert subagents
agy.install: install the Google Antigravity CLI (native binary, typically ~/.local/bin/agy)
agy.auth: run agy once to complete the Antigravity OAuth flow

kimi.name: Kimi
kimi.description: Moonshot Kimi models via the Kimi Code CLI - specialized expert subagents
kimi.install: install Kimi Code; it lands in ~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi
kimi.auth: set an api_key in ~/.kimi-code/config.toml or export KIMI_API_KEY; `kimi login` covers the subscription device-code flow, which was not open for signup as of 2026-08-17

copilot.name: Copilot (GPT, Claude & Gemini)
copilot.description: GitHub Copilot GPT, Claude, and Gemini models via Copilot CLI - specialized expert subagents

grok.name: Grok
grok.description: xAI Grok models via the Grok CLI - specialized expert subagents
grok.install: install the Grok CLI; its stable launcher is ~/.grok/bin/grok on Unix and ~\.grok\bin\grok.exe on Windows; some Unix installs also expose ~/.local/bin/grok as a symlink
grok.auth: `grok login` (grok.com account). A free account has a usage limit that returns a JSON error object rather than an exit code.
avoid: delegating into a repository you do not control: project instruction files in cwd are auto-loaded with no off switch

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.description: Cursor-hosted models via the Cursor Agent CLI - specialized expert subagents
cursor.install: install the Cursor Agent CLI; on Unix it lands in ~/.local/bin/cursor-agent as a symlink into ~/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/<version>/. The Windows install directory is not yet measured on any host here, so the bridge ships no Windows fallback rather than a guessed one.
cursor.auth: `cursor-agent login` (Cursor account). Plan tier decides the model roster: the verified Free plan rejected every named third-party model, while `auto`, `composer-2.5`, and `composer-2.5-fast` completed live calls.
strengths: many model families behind one CLI
stable multi-turn resume that inherits its model
avoid: tasks needing enforced denial: --mode ask deflects but was defeated by an adversarial prompt, and there are no command-line deny rules. Route to Claude or Copilot for provider-enforced denial, Grok for its built-in write/shell deny rules, or a native Codex registration explicitly configured read-only
runs that must be reproducible on the default model: 'auto' is server-routed and resolved to two different models across one session
